chunks: 1154 - Muʿādh used to lead salat in a masjid during the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he would make the recitation lengthy.
And a man passed by him, and he began a long surah, so the man recited for himself and performed salat, then mounted his riding animal.

When that reached the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, he sent for Muʿādh and said: “O Muʿādh, beware lest you be one who causes hardship; adhere to ‘By the sun and its brightness’ and those like it.”

key_terms.سُورَةً طَوِيلَةً: a long chapter of the Qur'an
key_terms.فَتَّانًا: one who causes trial, hardship, or aversion for others
key_terms.مَسْجِدٍ: a mosque, the place where congregational salat is performed
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leads the people in salat as Imam
key_terms.ٱلشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا: the surah beginning with 'By the sun and its brightness,' cited as an example of shorter recitation

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say about making congregational prayer too long?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Muʿādh would lengthen the recitation in congregational salat, which caused difficulty for some worshippers. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم instructed him to recite shorter surahs, showing consideration and ease in leading communal prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1154 - Mu'adh used to lead prayer in a mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah (sw) and would make the recitation lengthy.
One day, a man passed by while Mu'adh was reciting a long Surah, so the man recited (the prayer) for himself, completed it, and then rode off on his mount.

When this incident reached The Prophet (sw), he sent for Mu'adh and said:
"O’ Mu'adh, be careful not to be a source of hardship (fitnah). Recite from the shorter Surahs like 'By the sun and its brightness' (Ash-Shams) and similar ones."
